item.title: Iran War Live Updates: One American Rescued From Fighter Jet Downed Over Iran, Officials Say
item.summary: The fate of a second airman shot down in a F-15E warplane was unknown. It was the first time during the five-week war that a U.S. warplane had been brought down over Iran.

item.title: Rima Hassan Is Charged With Glorifying Terrorism Online in Social Media Post
item.summary: Rima Hassan, a member of the European Parliament, could face seven years in prison for the post, in which she quoted a perpetrator of a 1972 massacre in Israel.

item.title: Myanmar Junta Chief Ascends to President, Five Years After Coup
item.summary: U Min Aung Hlaing’s elevation to the civilian post is the conclusion of elections in the country, which were stage managed by the military.

item.title: At War With Iran Again, Some Israelis Fear Conflict Is Becoming Routine
item.summary: A majority of Israelis support the war with Iran, but many doubt that it will solve Israel’s long-term security problems. Some also question their prime minister’s assurances and motives.

item.title: As H-1B Visa Program Changes, Skilled Foreign Workers Consider Leaving U.S.
item.summary: As the Trump administration cracks down on the H-1B visa program, which allows skilled workers like software engineers to work in the United States, foreign professionals are debating whether to stay and build careers or quit the American Dream.

item.title: Kuwait Blames Iran for Attack on Power and Desalination Plants
item.summary: In Kuwait, an Iranian attack on Friday damaged a power and water desalination plant, officials said. Both sides in the Iran war have ramped up strikes on civilian targets.

item.title: In a Muzzled Russia, He Still Speaks His Mind
item.summary: While hundreds of other journalists fled into exile after Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dmitri A. Muratov stayed. But he did not stay quiet.

item.title: In Syria, Kidnappings of Women and Girls Fuel a Minority Group’s Fears
item.summary: A Times investigation found that abductions of women and girls from Syria’s Alawite minority were more common, and more brutal, than the government has acknowledged.

item.title: After Sting Operation, Cousin of Bashar al-Assad Convicted in Arms for Drugs Deal
item.summary: The cousin, Antoine Kassis, was found guilty of conspiracy to support a terrorist group, after trying to sell weapons from the fallen regime to a Colombian militia.

item.title: What U.S. military Pilots Are Trained to Do if Shot Down
